items.title: Artificial intelligence for the diagnosis of malocclusion in children and adolescents: a systematic review of diagnostic accuracy with an exploratory meta-analysis
items.authors: Sun B
items.conclusion: AI-based diagnosis of malocclusion in children and adolescents appears to be promising, but currently, the evidence is limited, of low certainty, and insufficient for widespread use in clinical practice; for now, AI should be used in addition to clinicians' judgement. Larger, standardised diagnostic accuracy studies reporting complete 2 × 2 data are required.

items.title: Effect of zinc-modified dental implants on osseointegration outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of preclinical animal studies
items.authors: Alenezi A
items.conclusion: Within the limitations of the available data from preclinical studies, implant surfaces modified with zinc were associated with improved histomorphometric indicators of osseointegration. However, there were significant methodological variations among the studies and lack of evidence of clinical relevance and hence a need for well-designed clinical studies.

items.title: Chlorhexidine mouthwash for oral hygiene maintenance in orthodontic patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
items.authors: Dashti AI, Almutairi AR, Alomran Y et al.
items.conclusion: CHX mouthwash, particularly at 0.2% concentration, provides short-term adjunctive benefits for plaque control and gingival inflammation in orthodontic patients. However, high heterogeneity and potential adverse effects support selective, time-limited use rather than routine prescription.

items.title: Restorative Management of Medium to Large Molar Defects Associated with Post Eruptive Enamel Breakdown in Molar- Incisor Hypomineralisation: An Umbrella Review
items.authors: Daniele S, Al-Nabulsi MH
items.conclusion: Treatment of medium and large MIH defects should be individualized according to enamel quality, patient cooperation, and eruption stage. Adhesive composite resin restorations remain the firstline approach where feasible, while HV-GICs offer a valid alternative for selective and minimally invasive management of MIH defect. Overall, the quality of evidence is moderate to low, highlighting the need for well-designed randomized clinical trials and…

items.title: Relevance of Silk Sutures in Contemporary Dental Practice: A Narrative Review
items.authors: Umamaheswaran I, Pathak V, Balachandar K et al.

items.title: Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea: a multidimensional clinical framework for diagnosis and treatment-a narrative review
items.authors: Pavone M, Verrillo E, Laguardia M et al.
items.conclusion: The proposed multidimensional clinical framework integrates physiological and clinical characteristics to support phenotype-informed, individualized management, linking assessment to targeted or combined interventions and reassessment of persistent disease.

items.title: Beyond clear aligners: A lifecycle framework for micro- and nanoplastic exposure in orthodontics: A narrative review
items.journal: Journal of the World federation of orthodontists
items.authors: Firinciogullari EC, Vaiid N, Yadav S et al.
items.conclusion: We highlight that the field remains methodologically immature and that particle detection should not be equated with clinical disease. A structured orthodontic framework is needed to distinguish documented microscale release from inferred nanoscale risk, to interrogate workflow‑dependent biocompatibility, and to guide safer material design, clinical protocols, waste collection, recycling strategies, and future exposure studies.

items.title: Adjunctive benefits of host modulation to non-surgical periodontal therapy: A systematic review, meta-analysis, meta-regression, and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
items.authors: Issa AW, Parma-Benfenati L, Hazrati P et al.
items.conclusion: Although currently available evidence is inconsistent, SDD or omega-3 may complement NSPT when systemically administered for ≥6 months in healthy patients but not in diabetics.

items.title: Solid platelet-rich fibrin versus connective tissue graft for root coverage procedures: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
items.authors: Pacer M, Colognese MRV, Jassniker VB et al.
items.conclusion: Although CTG remains the most predictable approach for modifying the periodontal phenotype and gaining keratinized tissue, solid PRF represents a clinically viable alternative that may offer patient-centered benefits by avoiding palatal graft harvesting, particularly for patients with an adequate baseline periodontal phenotype.

items.title: Association Between Low-Carbohydrate Diets and Periodontitis: Results From a Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study Using NHANES 2009-2014 Data
items.authors: Xu X, Zeng F, Bao D et al.
items.conclusion: In exploratory subgroup analyses, potential interactions were observed for smoking (p interaction = 0.024), physical activity (p interaction = 0.004), and hypertension (p interaction = 0.038). Our results suggest that the relationship between LCDs and periodontitis depends on the quality and types of macronutrients consumed.

items.title: Association Between Rheumatoid Arthritis Disease Duration and Periodontal Health: A Retrospective Observational Study
items.authors: Swathi D, Godasi SP, Jamatia K et al.
items.conclusion: These findings highlight the potential value of integrating periodontal evaluation into the routine management of patients with prolonged RA. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between RA duration and periodontal deterioration.

items.title: Laboratory study on AgNPs-modified 4-META/MMA-TBB resin as an antibacterial adhesive for root fracture reattachment
items.authors: Guo J, Fang Z, Liu X et al.
items.conclusion: AgNPs incorporation did not impair the fracture resistance of roots reattached with 4-META/MMA-TBB resin, whereas MNZ reduced it dose-dependently. AgNPs-modified 4-META/MMA-TBB resin is a promising antibacterial adhesive to improve the outcomes of root fracture reattachment.

items.title: Preoperative information-seeking behavior and perioperative experiences in patients undergoing periodontal mucogingival surgery: a single-center cross-sectional survey
items.authors: Luo W, Pan R, Liu S et al.
items.conclusion: Education level showed an exploratory association with professional information seeking among patients who had undergone mucogingival surgery. Statistical associations were also observed among recalled preoperative anxiety, postoperative reactions, and reported decision-making influences. Their relevance to preoperative communication requires prospective evaluation.

items.conclusion: The semi-digital workflow represents a clinically applicable and reproducible alternative for fabricating custom-fit EVA mouthguards in patients undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment. Virtual planning of orthodontic relief may facilitate individualized adaptation of the mouthguard to the orthodontic appliances, although clinical assessment and periodic reassessment remain essential throughout active orthodontic treatment.

items.title: A Theory-Guided Feasibility Study of Using a Minimum Dataset to Improve Routine Recording of Traumatic Dental Injuries

items.authors: Kenny KP, Owen J, DiMartino E et al.
items.conclusion: Recording many of the clinician and patient outcomes for the MDS-TDI is feasible and acceptable to dentists working in a tertiary referral centre. Further work is required to explore what is feasible to record in dental primary care.

items.authors: Okolo CC, Amole TG

items.authors: Sofar MK, Abid MF, AlHakeem K et al.

Most Iraqi orthodontists like using distalizers for correction of Class II malocclusions in permanent dentition. Skeletal anchorage intra-alveolar molar distalization devices are more preferred. items.title: Biochemical analysis of the impact of glycemic control on inducible nitric oxide synthase and proinflammatory cytokine levels in the gingival tissues of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and periodontitis
items.authors: Odyakmaz SZ, Bolat SY, Acarel EE
items.conclusion: Poor glycemic control was associated with an enhanced inflammatory response, whereas well-controlled T2DM participants presented inflammatory profiles similar to those of systemically healthy participants.

items.title: Association of light BioAge with edentulism risk in middle-aged and elderly people: a retrospective cohort study
items.authors: Li Y
items.conclusion: A high BioAge was associated with an elevated risk of edentulism among middle-aged and elderly people, especially for individuals whose light BioAge exceeds their chronological age.

items.title: Comparison of mid-palatal suture morphology via suture bone densities between unilateral cleft lip and palate with non-cleft individuals using python programming language
items.authors: Huqh MZU, Yaacob HB, Selvaraj S et al.
items.conclusion: Children with the UCLP group had lower palatal bone density compared to the NC group, indicating defective MPS fusion. These results highlight the need for individualized treatment planning for orthodontic treatment and maxillary expansion in children with clefts.

items.authors: Zeng J, Zhang C, Luo P et al.
items.conclusion: This study reveals that hypoxia induces targeted m6A epitranscriptomic remodeling in DPSCs. We propose a putative regulatory axis where hypoxia-upregulated IGF2BP1 may facilitate cellular adaptation by stabilizing transcripts associated with angiogenesis and tissue regeneration. Our findings suggest these genes may serve as pivotal regulators of the hypoxic response in DPSCs, representing a novel mechanism for adaptation. While these results…

items.title: Lymphocyte Reactivity to Metal-Containing Test Preparations in a Selected Scoliosis Cohort: A Retrospective Case Series of MELISA Results and Reported Metal Exposures
items.authors: Dutton R, Bjørklund G
items.conclusion: With no scoliosis-free comparison group or systematically verified clinical allergy outcomes, the results describe heterogeneous in vitro reactivity in a small, self-selected cohort; they do not establish clinical metal allergy, increased reactivity in scoliosis, or causation. Controlled studies are needed to assess clinical relevance.

items.title: Three-dimensional characterization of differential labial gingival surface changes at labial protuberance sites following orthodontic tooth movement
items.authors: Yoon HR, Choi EA, Sreng Y et al.
items.conclusion: LP sites predominantly corresponded to pretreatment interdental regions and showed less labial gingival displacement than adjacent mesial tooth-covering sites. Localized differences in tooth movement may be associated with LP occurrence.

items.title: What is the level of hypodontia service provision in secondary care in the UK? A cross-sectional study
items.authors: Johal A, Alajmi S, Dean R
items.conclusion: Common challenges included workforce shortages, funding constraints, long waiting times and difficulties coordinating MDT care.Conclusions Considerable variation was observed in hypodontia service provision across the UK. National guidance, a minimum dataset and a registry may support more optimal care and service evaluation.

items.authors: Wang H, Pham C, Kurniyati K et al.
items.conclusion: Tissue microarrays detect internalin antigens in HNSCC specimens, supporting their in vivo relevance. Together, these findings establish a direct mechanistic link between an oral pathogen and HNSCC progression and extend the paradigm of internalin-E-cadherin interactions from microbial pathogenesis to cancer biology.
